thread.title: City of Covington launches interactive platform highlighting over 140 pieces of public art
thread.title_full: City of Covington launches interactive platform highlighting over 140 pieces of public art

author: D. S. Young
title: City of Covington launches interactive platform highlighting over 140 pieces of public art
text:
The City of Covington has launched an interactive online project that highlights over 140 public art installations throughout the city. The initiative provides residents and visitors with a way to explore murals, sculptures, architectural details, and other forms of public art located in various neighborhoods.
In recent years, Covington’s public art scene has received attention both nationally and regionally. Local media have covered the city’s creative offerings, and notable works such as Clive—a 30-foot extraterrestrial figure at the Midtown Parking Garage—are now featured in Kentucky’s statewide tourism guide.
Recognizing a lack of a centralized inventory for its public art collection, the city developed this project to create a comprehensive dataset documenting artistic assets and preserving their histories. The online catalog includes information about each artwork, its creator, and the story behind it.
“Art is a vital part of Covington’s identity,” said Kaitlin Bryan, Regulatory Services Manager & Historic Preservation Specialist for the City. “It reflects the City’s history, creativity, and sense of community. From international artists to local creatives, art here lives in our streets, throughout our neighborhoods, integrated into our city’s fabric.”
The new resource is intended to assist organizations interested in arts research or cultural planning as well as those developing public art tours. It also serves residents seeking to discover more about art in their communities.
Residents and visitors are encouraged to contribute by uploading photos of public artworks through an online submission form. Each submission will be reviewed by city staff before being added to the site.
The project was created with support from ArtsWave and meetNKY. Both organizations partnered with the city to help identify installations and provide background information on artworks.
“This new public art collection promises to elevate Covington’s creative landscape even further. An accessible, interactive inventory like this strengthens research, cultural planning and can even help highlight Covington’s commitment to public art during major regional moments like next year’s BLINK event,” said Rachael Parker, Director of Northern Kentucky Creative Placemaking for ArtsWave. “It also supports ArtsWave’s mission of bringing people together by making it easier for residents and visitors to experience both sides of the river as part of one connected, vibrant community.”
Adebukola Aderanti, an intern with Covington’s Economic Development Department, played a significant role in moving the project forward.
